page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 24 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1572.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0. However, multi-core and memory performance metrics fall into the lower tiers. The stress-ng multi-core CPU score is 4147.67, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2855.0, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show 28.26 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 24.11 GB/sec for large block write operations. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 26.8 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.09 GB/sec perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 18.77 GB/sec.

The c2-standard-4 is designed for compute-bound workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU resources and high clock speeds, such as single-threaded processing, basic text processing, and lightweight LLM text generation. However, its weak multi-core scaling, lower database operations score of 1545.89 on Passmark, and weak Redis SET performance of 4.1 million operations per second make it less suitable for heavy multi-threaded databases, intensive software compilation, or high-throughput web serving. It offers a dedicated compute profile without the overhead of local storage, making it a qualitative entry point for compute-focused tasks requiring consistent CPU allocation.
